program: Wingless fixed-budget future-data learning-curve mechanism attribution
question: Which concrete prediction-path mechanism explains the large cross-domain difference in cumulative adaptation gain observed in R11 under identical fixed budgets?
hypothesis: Replay the exact R11 three leave-one-domain-out arms, 15,819-byte non-target training budget, 256-motif capacity, 1,454-byte target window, 872-byte adaptation stream, eight 109-byte cumulative packets, 582-byte sealed evaluation suffix, and deterministic R10/R11 predictor. Add attribution only. For every evaluation prediction at every packet, compare packet0 and adapted predictions and assign exactly one frozen category: motif_admission (target 4-byte motif absent from packet0 selected set and present after adaptation), motif_eviction (present at packet0 and absent after adaptation), motif_successor_refinement (present in both but selected motif best successor changes), baseline_byte_refinement (motif absent in both and byte-baseline prediction changes), or prediction_unchanged. Record signed hit delta (-1/0/+1) per category. Category net gains must exactly reconstruct each arm's R11 cumulative adaptation gain: code=210, structured=98, technical_prose=103. Define code_excess_gain = code gain - mean(other two)=109.5. The dominant mechanism is the non-unchanged category with largest code category net gain minus mean(other-domain category net gain). This is retrospective mechanism attribution only; it cannot allocate data, change the predictor, or retain any mechanism.

portfolio_context.role: advisory-only; characterize fixed-budget future-data learning before proposing policy

prior_evidence.interpretation: No preregistered training-only signal reliably orders learning efficiency; directly attribute the adaptation-gain mechanism before proposing allocation.

external_authority.execution_host_policy: GitHub-hosted compute only; host distinct from LINKDEADKB

attribution.signed_delta: adapted_correct - packet0_correct for the same evaluation position
attribution.accounting_rule: sum category signed deltas per arm must equal that arm's R11 cumulative_adaptation_gain
attribution.dominant_rule: among first four categories, maximize code_category_net_gain - mean(structured_category_net_gain, technical_prose_category_net_gain)

classification_rules.supported: Validity passes and one frozen prediction-path category explains at least 50% of the code-vs-other cumulative-gain excess, with exact transition accounting.
classification_rules.mixed: Validity passes and at least one category has positive code excess but no category reaches 50%.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but no category has positive code excess despite the replayed R11 gain difference.
classification_rules.invalid: Any parent, authority, source, budget, split, R11 replay identity, transition categorization/accounting, determinism, capacity, provenance, or qualification criterion fails.

successor_if_supported.intent: test a bounded no-self-modification data-allocation policy targeted to the attributed mechanism on a new preregistered split; compare against equal allocation under the same fixed total data budget

successor_if_mixed_or_negative.intent: factor interacting admission/refinement pathways before proposing any data-allocation policy

no_post_result_tuning_rule: Do not alter R11 data/budgets/splits/capacity, predictor, transition categories, R11 replay totals, code-excess definition, dominant rule, 50% criterion, metrics, classification, or authority after primary output.
